meta.title: Active Directory PowerShell commands: cheatsheet
meta.description: Active Directory cheatsheet: Get-ADUser, Search-ADAccount, replication, GPO, dcdiag and FSMO, with required rights, examples and common pitfalls.
meta.intro: ActiveDirectory (RSAT) module cmdlets and command-line tools to administer and troubleshoot a domain: accounts, groups, replication, GPOs, domain controllers.
meta.card: Get-ADUser, Search-ADAccount, groups, replication, GPO, dcdiag, FSMO: copy-ready examples and common pitfalls.

top.title: Prerequisites
top.note: Install the RSAT tools once (Windows 11), then import the module.

items.note: Checks the connection to the domain.

meta.notice: Test with -WhatIf first when it exists. AD changes replicate to every domain controller: prefer a test organizational unit.

entries.name: Get-ADUser
entries.desc: Reads one or more user accounts.
entries.pitfall: Without -Properties, only basic properties are returned; LastLogonDate is replicated only approximately (use lastLogon on each DC for accuracy).

entries.name: New-ADUser
entries.desc: Creates a user account.
ex: New-ADUser -Name 'Jean Dupont' -GivenName Jean -Surname Dupont -SamAccountName jdupont -UserPrincipalName jdupont@contoso.local -Path 'OU=Employes,DC=contoso,DC=local' -AccountPassword (Read-Host -AsSecureString 'Mot de passe') -Enabled $true -ChangePasswordAtLogon $true
entries.perms: Delegation 'Create user objects' on the OU
entries.pitfall: Without -Enabled $true the account stays disabled; the password must meet the domain policy.

entries.name: Set-ADUser
entries.desc: Changes a user's attributes (department, title, manager, expiration).
entries.perms: Write delegation on the attributes concerned
entries.pitfall: For an attribute not covered by a parameter, use -Replace / -Add / -Clear with a hash table.

entries.name: Unlock-ADAccount
entries.desc: Unlocks an account locked after too many wrong passwords.
entries.pitfall: The lockout repeats if a device keeps an old password: find the source with event 4740.

entries.name: Set-ADAccountPassword
entries.desc: Resets an account's password.
entries.pitfall: Never pass the password in clear text in a command: it would stay in the history.

entries.name: Search-ADAccount
entries.desc: Finds locked, disabled, inactive or password-expired accounts.
entries.pitfall: The -TimeSpan format is days.hours:minutes:seconds (90.00:00:00).

entries.name: Disable-ADAccount
entries.desc: Disables an account (when someone leaves); Enable-ADAccount re-enables it.
entries.pitfall: In a hybrid environment, disabling only reaches Entra ID at the next sync cycle.

entries.name: Get-ADGroupMember
entries.desc: Lists a group's members, including nested groups with -Recursive.
entries.pitfall: Fails beyond 5,000 members (web service limit): use Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter with memberOf.

entries.name: Add-ADGroupMember
entries.desc: Adds members to a group; Remove-ADGroupMember removes them.
entries.perms: Write access on the group's membership
entries.pitfall: The new member only sees the access at their next sign-in (Kerberos token).

entries.name: Get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership
entries.desc: Lists the groups a user or computer belongs to.
ex: Get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership jdupont | Select Name,GroupCategory | Sort Name
entries.pitfall: Only returns direct groups; for full nesting, use whoami /groups in the user's session.

entries.name: New-ADGroup
entries.desc: Creates a security or distribution group.
entries.perms: Group creation delegation on the OU
entries.pitfall: AGDLP rule: users in global groups, global groups in domain local groups, permissions on the latter.

entries.name: Get-ADComputer
entries.desc: Reads computer accounts (operating system, last logon).
ex: Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties OperatingSystem,LastLogonDate | Group OperatingSystem | Select Count,Name
entries.pitfall: Define $date = (Get-Date).AddDays(-90) before the filter; the variable does not exist by default.

entries.name: Reset-ComputerMachinePassword
entries.desc: Repairs the trust relationship of a domain member machine (run it on the machine).
entries.perms: Local elevated prompt and a domain account
entries.pitfall: Symptom: 'The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed'.

entries.name: Move-ADObject
entries.desc: Moves a user, computer or group to another OU.
entries.perms: Rights on the source and the destination
entries.pitfall: If 'Protect from accidental deletion' is on for the object, remove it first (Set-ADObject -ProtectedFromAccidentalDeletion $false).

entries.name: repadmin /replsummary
entries.desc: AD replication summary and forcing synchronization between domain controllers.
entries.pitfall: An 8453 (access denied) or 1722 (RPC) error points to rights, DNS or the firewall between the DCs.

entries.name: dcdiag
entries.desc: Full diagnostic of a domain controller (DNS, replication, FSMO, services).
entries.pitfall: A DNS failure is the most frequent cause: first check that the DC points to itself or another DC for DNS.

entries.name: netdom query fsmo / Get-ADForest
entries.desc: Identifies the controllers holding the five FSMO roles.
entries.pitfall: If a holding DC is lost for good, you must seize the role and never bring that DC back.

entries.name: Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole
entries.desc: Transfers an FSMO role to another domain controller.
entries.perms: Enterprise or schema administrator depending on the role
entries.pitfall: Transfer (both DCs online) and seizure (-Force, original DC lost) are two different operations.

entries.name: Get-ADDomainController
entries.desc: Lists the domain controllers and their roles.
entries.pitfall: -Discover uses DNS: if the result is wrong, check the SRV records.

entries.name: Get-ADReplicationFailure
entries.desc: Replication failures of a domain controller.
entries.pitfall: Run it on a machine that sees every DC (RPC ports, 9389 ADWS).

entries.name: Get-GPO
entries.desc: Lists Group Policy objects.
entries.pitfall: GPOs that are created but not linked apply to nothing: check the link with Get-GPInheritance.

entries.name: Get-GPOReport
entries.desc: Exports the content of one or all GPOs as an HTML or XML report.
entries.pitfall: Useful to compare or archive before a change; also back up with Backup-GPO.

entries.name: New-GPLink
entries.desc: Links a GPO to an organizational unit, a site or the domain.
entries.perms: Right to link GPOs on the target
entries.pitfall: A GPO applied to a whole domain also affects the domain controllers: test on a pilot OU first.

entries.name: Invoke-GPUpdate
entries.desc: Forces GPO application on a remote machine (equivalent of gpupdate /force).
entries.perms: Local administrator on the target, firewall that allows remote management
entries.pitfall: By default, a random delay of up to 10 minutes applies; add -RandomDelayInMinutes 0.

entries.name: Backup-GPO
entries.desc: Backs up GPOs (and Restore-GPO to put them back).
entries.perms: Read access to GPOs; write access to restore
entries.pitfall: The backup does not contain the links to OUs: note them with Get-GPInheritance.

entries.name: Get-ADObject (AD Recycle Bin)
entries.desc: Finds and restores a deleted object when the AD Recycle Bin is enabled.
entries.pitfall: Without the AD Recycle Bin enabled (Enable-ADOptionalFeature 'Recycle Bin Feature'), restoring attributes is limited.

entries.name: Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
entries.desc: The domain password policy and fine-grained policies.
entries.pitfall: A fine-grained policy (PSO) takes precedence over the domain policy for the targeted users.

entries.name: Get-ADUser (audit: never-logged-on accounts, old passwords)
entries.desc: Common audit queries on accounts.
ex: Get-ADUser -Filter {Enabled -eq $true} -Properties PasswordLastSet | Where PasswordLastSet -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-365) | Select Name,PasswordLastSet
entries.pitfall: AdminCount = 1 flags former or current privileged accounts; check their membership before cleaning up.

entries.name: ldifde / csvde
entries.desc: Exports or imports AD objects as CSV (csvde) or LDIF (ldifde).
entries.perms: Read access; write access for import
entries.pitfall: An import with -i can change the directory massively: always try it first with a small test file.
